covers.quote: Use italics and sentence case for film titles
Write the title as it appears in film information. Include punctuation marks and any intentional misspelling.

If the film is part of a series, include the number of the series in the same format as in the original title of the film. For example, if the original title has the number written as a word, use the word.

examples.note: Film title in italics and sentence case with year of production.

parts.quote: Ride like a girl (2019) tells the story of jockey Michelle Payne.

examples.note: Film title retaining roman numeral from original series title.

parts.quote: They released The man from Snowy River II in 1988.

rules.quote: Italicise the title and use sentence case.
rules.violation_condition: a film title not formatted in italics and sentence case, or not matching the film's original spelling and punctuation
when: Include punctuation marks and any intentional misspelling from the original film information.
If part of a series, format series numbers as in the original title (e.g. word vs numeral).
After the first mention, the title may be abbreviated.
rules.why: G-1, G-4: Merged heading and body instruction on film title styling.

covers.quote: If you mention the date in the text, you don’t have to include it in parentheses.
You can also omit the date in parentheses.

examples.note: Year placed in parentheses in roman type after italicised title.

parts.quote: Picnic at Hanging Rock (1975) helped to revive the Australian film industry in the 1970s.

rules.quote: Place this after the title in roman type and enclosed in parentheses.
rules.violation_condition: the year of production in an in-text film citation not placed after the title in parentheses and roman type (unless mentioned in the text)
when: Applies when including the year of production in in-text film citations.
Exception: If the date is mentioned directly in the running text, it does not need to be in parentheses.
Exception: After the first mention, the date in parentheses may be omitted.
rules.why: G-2, G-3: Covers date placement rule and its exceptions.

covers.quote: In a reference list, use the director and the year of release. Include the place of production if known. If there is no credited director, use the name of the producer.

examples.note: Standard reference list entry for a film.

parts.quote: Seet S (director) (2019) Storm boy [motion picture], Ambience Entertainment, Screen Australia, South Australian Film Corporation, Australia.

examples.note: Reference list entry using producer when director is not credited.

parts.quote: Jury WF (producer) (1916) Battle of the Somme [motion picture], British Topical Committee for War Films, London, UK.

rules.quote: Director D (director) or Producer P (producer) (Year) Title of film: subtitle of film [motion picture], Name of Studio or Publisher, Place of Production.
rules.violation_condition: a film reference list entry not structured according to the author-date film citation format
when: Use the director and year of release.
Include place of production if known.
If there is no credited director, use the producer.
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Body rule template defines author-date citation structure for films.

covers.quote: Use roman type and quotation marks for parts of works, such as episodes.
Place the names of episodes in quotation marks and roman type.

examples.note: Television episode in quotation marks, roman type, sentence case.

parts.quote: The Australian story episode ‘Out of the blue’ is about a shark attack in the Whitsundays.

rules.quote: Use sentence case, roman type and quotation marks for episodes of a program.
rules.violation_condition: an episode title of a television program not styled in sentence case, roman type, or enclosed in quotation marks
rules.why: G-4: Specific rule for television episode title styling.

covers.quote: Use roman type and the spelling and capitalisation that the company uses for the names of channels, streaming services and networks.

examples.note: Channel name in roman type without quotation marks.

parts.quote: Channel 7 has been screening cricket over the summer.

rules.quote:
Use roman type and no quotation marks for the names of:

- production companies
- networks
- channels
- streaming services.
rules.violation_condition: the name of a production company, network, channel, or streaming service placed in quotation marks or italics instead of plain roman type
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Direct instruction on formatting names of broadcast entities.

examples.note: Year range in roman type and parentheses.

parts.quote: One of the longest-running police dramas on Australian television was Homicide (1964–77).

rules.quote: Include the year of production of television programs in roman type and brackets.
rules.violation_condition: the year of production for a television program not set in roman type and brackets/parentheses
rules.why: Standalone rule for year format on television programs.

examples.note: Arabic numeral used for season.

parts.quote: Season 2 of Offspring introduced the character of Dr Patrick Reid.

examples.note: Roman numeral used for season.

parts.quote: Season II of Offspring introduced the character of Dr Patrick Reid.

rules.quote: Use arabic – not roman – numerals for the numbers of seasons.
rules.violation_condition: roman numerals used instead of arabic numerals for television season numbers
rules.why: Explicit contrast pair showing violating roman numerals.

covers.quote: In a reference list, include the name of the director or producer and the year of release. Include the place of production if known.
If the episode doesn’t have a name, write the name of the program first.

examples.note: Standard reference list entry for a television episode.

parts.quote: Pellizzeri R (director) (1994) ‘Luck of the draw’ [television program], Blue heelers (season 1, episode 44), Seven Network, Melbourne.

examples.note: Reference list entry when an episode has no individual title.

parts.quote: ABC Television (2019) Gardening Australia (season 30, episode 35) [television program], ABC Television, Sydney.

rules.quote: Director D (director) or Producer P (producer) (Year) ‘Title of episode: subtitle of episode’ [television program], Name of series (season number, episode number), Name of Station or Studio, Place of Production.
rules.violation_condition: a television program reference list entry not structured according to the author-date television citation format
when: Include director or producer name and year of release.
Include place of production if known.
If the episode doesn't have a name, write the name of the program first.
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Covers television reference list formatting template and variation.

covers.quote: Use italics for the titles of programs.
Write the year of production in parentheses. Use roman type after the title.
Enclose the names of individual episodes in single quotation marks and use roman type.
Use sentence case.

examples.note: Episode in single quotes/roman type, show title in italics, year in parentheses.

parts.quote: ‘The bilby, the moon and the Birriliburu Rangers’ from Off track went to air in January. One of the longest-running Australian radio programs was Blue hills (1949–76).

rules.quote: Italicise radio programs and use roman type for episodes

covers.quote: In a reference list, include the full date the episode went to air. Include the place of production if known.

examples.note: Standard reference list entry for a radio program.

parts.quote: Jones A (presenter) (18 January 2020) ‘The bilby, the moon and the Birriliburu Rangers’ [radio program], Off track, ABC Radio National, Sydney.

rules.quote: Presenter P (presenter) (Day Month Year) ‘Title of episode: subtitle of episode’ [radio program], Name of program, Name of Station or Studio, Place of Production.

when: Include the full date the episode went to air.
Include place of production if known.

covers.quote: Use italics for the name of the program series.
Use roman type and quotation marks for the names of individual podcast episodes.
Use sentence case.

examples.note: Podcast episode in quotation marks and roman type, show in italics.

rules.quote: Italicise podcast series and use roman type for episodes

covers.quote: Rule: Host H (host) and Producer P (producer) (Day Month Year) ‘Title of podcast: subtitle of podcast’ [podcast], Name of podcast, Name of Podcast Network, accessed Day Month Year.

examples.note: Reference list entry for a podcast accessed online with accessed date.

rules.quote: Hyperlink the episode’s title if you played it from a webpage. Don’t link to the podcast’s file name. Always link to the webpage that hosts the podcast episode. Include the date it was accessed at the end of the reference.

when: Applies to podcasts referenced from a webpage.
rules.why: G-2: Web linking and access date rules for podcast references.

covers.quote: Use italics and sentence case for published script titles.
Use roman type and quotation marks for unpublished script titles.

covers.quote: Reference the script as you would a book.

parts.quote: Carey P and Lawrence R (1985) Bliss: the screenplay, University of Queensland Press, St Lucia, Queensland.

rules.quote: Author A (Year) Title of script: subtitle of script, Name of Publisher, Place of Publication.
